final_text:
I couldn't run `python -m mockcheck --help` because the PowerShell call timed out, so I read the report directly. I took the 10 spike_P0 organisms from `truth/spike_manifest.tsv` and looked up each one's species-level (rank S) clade read count in `data/spike_P0.report.gz`. Each organism matched at most one species row.

| Organism (manifest) | Spiked pairs | Report clade reads (S) | Call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pseudomonas aeruginosa | 40,000 | 811 | detected |
| Escherichia coli | 4,000 | 72 | detected |
| Salmonella enterica | 400 | 4 | missed |
| Lactobacillus fermentum (shown in the report as Limosilactobacillus fermentum) | 40 | 26 | detected |
| Enterococcus faecalis | 40,000 | 6,457 | detected |
| Staphylococcus aureus | 4,000 | 54 | detected |
| Listeria monocytogenes | 400 | not in report | missed |
| Bacillus subtilis | 40 | 2 | missed |
| Saccharomyces cerevisiae | 40,000 | not in report | missed |
| Cryptococcus neoformans | 4,000 | not in report | missed |

Five of the ten added organisms reach the 10-read threshold. The counts in the report are far below the number of pairs spiked in, for every organism. Both fungi (Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Cryptococcus neoformans) are missing from the report entirely, even though S. cerevisiae was spiked at the highest level. That suggests the database used may not include fungi, but the report alone can't confirm that.
